sentences.text: The name Orkoraptor means "Toothed River thief," derived from the Aoniken word "Orr-Korr," the local name for the La Leona River.
This medium-sized theropod measured 8.4 meters long and weighed 1400 kilograms.
It possessed specialized teeth that were unserrated on the front side and had an 8-shaped cross section.
The genus Orkoraptor was described by Novas, Ezcurra, and Lecuona in 2008, based on the holotype specimen MPM-Pv 3457, which was excavated in 2001.
Original describers could not conclusively assign Orkoraptor to a specific family because many features contradicted those of coelurosaurs.
Subsequent studies recovered Orkoraptor within the clade Megaraptora.

Phylogenetic trees from the Gualicho shinyae publication suggest megaraptorans are either allosauroids or basal coelurosaurs, leading a 2009 study by Benson, Carrano, and Brusatte to classify Orkoraptor as an allosauroid within the family Neovenatoridae.
Orkoraptor lived during the late Cretaceous Period in southern Patagonia, Argentina, making it one of the most southerly known carnivorous dinosaurs in South America.

While originally thought to be from the Maastrichtian, the animal is now considered to date from the Cenomanian to Santonian, or approximately between 76 and 70 million years ago, with estimates ranging from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
